Nivel de vechime: Nivel mediu de experiență

Sectoare de activitate: Servicii de informații
Project overview 
 We are looking for an Embedded Hardware Integration Engineer to join our Randstad Digital Romanian Team in a new challenging project in the automotive field.
 You will own the reliability, scalability, and readiness of the hardware lab for development and validation activities. This role connects embedded software with real automotive hardware by ensuring that shared evaluation and reference boards, rack infrastructure, and remote-access equipment are correctly installed, configured, and constantly available for the Linux BSP engineering teams.
 Meet our client 
 Our client is a world leader in secure connectivity solutions for embedded applications, driving innovation in the secure connected vehicle, end-to-end security & privacy and smart connected solutions markets. Built on more than 60 years of combined experience and expertise, our client has employees in more than 35 countries.
 Responsibilities: 
Install, rack, cable, label, and maintain automotive development boards, power-control units, network switches, serial-access devices, USB-SD-MUX devices, debuggers, and supporting servers.
Prepare and reconfigure board setups for development, CI, and automation use cases, including boot-mode selection, jumpers, DIP switches, storage media, and non-standard cabling.
Perform first-level diagnosis and repair of unstable setups, damaged cables, power issues, serial-access problems, storage-media failures, and connectivity faults; coordinate replacement or specialist support when needed.
Enable reliable remote power cycle/reset, serial console access, image deployment, and board reservation for shared hardware.
Integrate boards with existing lab and test infrastructure and support interfaces used by CI/CD and automated test campaigns.
Work with test automation and CI engineers to reproduce setup-related failures, distinguish infrastructure faults from software defects, and restore service quickly.
Own the accuracy of the hardware inventory, setup identifiers, network addressing, cabling maps, board revisions, accessories, ownership, and operational status.
Create and maintain setup guides, recovery procedures, known-issue notes, and photographs or diagrams for supported hardware configurations.
Partner with Linux BSP development, testing, IT infrastructure, and security teams.
Support new-product introduction and first-silicon activities by preparing setups needed for remote work and continuous automated testing.
 Requirements: 
At least 3 years of work experience in a similar role.
Experience in Embedded Hardware Lab Operations & Debugging.
Work experience with Embedded Linux & Command Line.
Automotive Board & Setup Enablement.
CI/CD & Lab Automation Integration.
Hands-on experience in an electronics, embedded systems, validation, test, or engineering lab environment.
Practical knowledge of embedded development boards, power supplies, serial consoles, storage media, Ethernet networking, and common lab cabling.
Experience debugging and troubleshooting hardware issues using multimeters, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers to diagnose electrical, signal integrity, and communication problems.
Comfortable working in Linux from the command line, including SSH, file transfer, logs, permissions, networking checks, and basic shell scripting.
Ability to read board documentation, schematics, or connection diagrams and translate them into a working, repeatable setup.
Structured troubleshooting approach and the discipline to document symptoms, evidence, configuration, and resolution.
Electrical/electronics, computer engineering, automation, telecommunications, or a comparable technical education, or equivalent practical experience.
Good command of English, speaking and writing.
 Nice to have: 
Automotive processors or S32 platforms, such as S32N, S32G, or S32R.
Embedded Linux and boot-flow familiarity, including U-Boot, Linux kernel, Yocto-based images, and serial-console diagnostics.
Lab automation equipment and interfaces such as programmable PDUs, USB-SD-MUX, relay/GPIO controllers, CAN interfaces, network-controlled switches, or Lauterbach debuggers.
CI/CD or automated test environments, particularly Jenkins-based pipelines and board farms.
Previous experience with Proxmox.
Python or advanced shell scripting for monitoring, provisioning, or repetitive lab operations.
Basic Git, issue tracking, and service-management workflows; exposure to Jira or ServiceNow is useful.
Networking fundamentals including DHCP, DNS, VLANs, routing, firewall constraints, TCP/IP troubleshooting, and packet capture.
 Benefits 
Attractive salary package according to your experience and seniority bonus;
The 13th salary depending on company’s performance;
Bonus for internal recommendations;
Meal tickets;
Private health insurance, including dental services and psychological consultations;
Flexible working hours (core-hours system);
Access to over 600 sports centers in the 7Card network;
Online language courses: English and French;
Access to the e-learning platform;
Access to technical training programs / workshops, as well as other technical events (both as a participant and as a speaker);
Development opportunities through involvement in internship & mentoring programs;
Access to soft-skills programs and workshops;
Access to various internal events and team-buildings;
Access to international opportunities for career development with challenging and exciting projects in a dynamic international working environment;
Paid days off offered for involvement in volunteering activities and for bank holidays occasion.
 Kindly note that only suitable candidates will be contacted.
